subject: paediatrics
title: Childhood Asthma, Stepwise Therapy and Cystic Fibrosis

steps.tx: Chronic airway inflammation drives variable expiratory airflow limitation and bronchial hyperresponsiveness. The diagnosis of **childhood asthma** relies upon recognizing recurrent episodes of wheezing, breathlessness, chest tightness, and nighttime cough triggered by viral infections, exercise, cold air, or aeroallergens. In children aged five years and older, spirometry demonstrates reversible airflow obstruction, defined as an increase in forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) of twelve percent or greater after bronchodilator inhalation.
steps.say: Childhood asthma features recurrent wheeze, breathlessness, and nocturnal cough triggered by viral infections or exercise. Spirometry shows twelve percent or greater FEV1 reversibility after salbutamol.

vis.caption: Clinical signs of acute childhood asthma exacerbation including pulsus paradoxus, tachypnoea, and silent chest. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Inhaled corticosteroid aerosol deposition in young children requires appropriate interface devices. The optimal delivery technique utilizes a **pressurized metered-dose inhaler spacer**, which decelerates high-velocity aerosol particles, reduces oral impaction, and maximizes intrapulmonary alveolar deposition. Children under four years require a spacer paired with a silicone face mask, while children aged four and older use a mouthpiece, taking five to six tidal breaths per puff.
steps.say: A metered-dose inhaler with a spacer is the best delivery device for children, decreasing throat deposition and improving lung delivery. Children under four use a mask; older children use a mouthpiece.

left.title: Spacer with Face Mask (<4 Years)
points: Tight seal over nose and mouth without leaks
Child takes 5 to 6 normal tidal breaths per puff
Wash face and rinse mouth after corticosteroid
Never actuate multiple puffs into spacer at once

right.title: Spacer with Mouthpiece (>=4 Years)
points: Lips closed tightly around mouthpiece
Slow deep inhalation followed by 10-second breath-hold
Higher intrapulmonary deposition than face mask
Avoids facial steroid deposition and cataracts

steps.tx: International guidelines structure chronic pharmacological management according to control levels. Global Initiative for Asthma outlines **stepwise asthma therapy**: Step 1 utilizes as-needed low-dose inhaled corticosteroids or SABA; Step 2 establishes daily maintenance low-dose inhaled corticosteroids (fluticasone or budesonide) or montelukast; Step 3 adds a long-acting beta2-agonist (LABA) or increases to medium-dose corticosteroids; and Steps 4 and 5 incorporate high-dose therapies and biological agents.
steps.say: Stepwise asthma management advances from as-needed relievers to daily low-dose inhaled steroids, adding long-acting beta agonists if control is incomplete. Regular review guides step-down.

rows: Medium-dose ICS alone or ICS + LTRA

steps.tx: Exocrine epithelial transport defects provoke multi-organ viscid secretions and chronic lung damage. The autosomal recessive disorder **cystic fibrosis CFTR defect** results from mutations in the Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance Regulator gene on chromosome 7q31, most commonly the delta-F508 deletion. Defective apical chloride and bicarbonate conductance with hyperabsorption of sodium dehydrates airway surface liquid, producing thick, tenacious mucus that cripples mucociliary clearance.
steps.say: Cystic fibrosis stems from CFTR chloride channel mutations on chromosome 7, usually delta-F508. Dehydrated, viscous secretions cause bronchiectasis, pancreatic failure, and meconium ileus.

vis.alt: Multisystem pathology of pediatric cystic fibrosis across lungs, pancreas, liver, and intestine.
vis.caption: Cystic fibrosis organ pathology illustrating bronchiectasis, pancreatic exocrine atrophy, and meconium ileus. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Neonatal presentation frequently features distal intestinal obstruction secondary to inspissated meconium. Approximately twenty percent of newborns with cystic fibrosis present with **meconium ileus obstruction**, characterized by abdominal distension, bilious emesis, and failure to pass meconium within forty-eight hours of birth. Contrast enema demonstrates a pathognomonic microcolon with pellets of inspissated meconium in the distal ileum, relieved by water-soluble diatrizoate meglumine enemas.
steps.say: Meconium ileus presents in twenty percent of newborns with cystic fibrosis as bilious vomiting and obstipation. Contrast enemas show a microcolon with impacted meconium pellets.

left.title: Meconium Ileus Signs
points: Failure to pass meconium by 48 hours
Distended loops of bowel with ground-glass soap bubble sign
Contrast enema shows unused, narrow microcolon
Therapeutic gastrografin enema or surgical enterostomy

right.title: Post-Neonatal Gastrointestinal Signs
points: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency in 85%
Malabsorptive steatorrhoea and severe failure to thrive
Rectal prolapse in toddlers secondary to bulky stools
Deficiency of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K)

steps.tx: Stimulated sweat electrolyte quantification provides the gold standard laboratory confirmation of cystic fibrosis. Performing the **pilocarpine iontophoresis sweat test** stimulates localized eccrine sweating using pilocarpine, collecting sweat on filter paper for coulometric chloride analysis. A sweat chloride concentration of sixty millimoles per litre or greater on two separate occasions definitively confirms cystic fibrosis, while thirty to fifty-nine millimoles per litre represents an intermediate borderline result.
steps.say: Quantitative pilocarpine sweat testing is the gold standard for cystic fibrosis. Sweat chloride of sixty millimoles per litre or greater on two occasions confirms the diagnosis.

steps.tx: Chronic endobronchial bacterial colonization dictates pulmonary disease progression and ultimate life expectancy. Initial childhood airway colonization with Staphylococcus aureus and Haemophilus influenzae is superseded by chronic **Pseudomonas aeruginosa colonization**, which transitions into an alginate-producing mucoid phenotype forming antibiotic-resistant biofilms. Chronic infection accelerates bronchiectasis and respiratory decline, requiring aggressive eradication protocols with inhaled tobramycin or nebulized colistin.
steps.say: Mucoid Pseudomonas aeruginosa colonizes cystic fibrosis airways, forming thick biofilms that drive bronchiectasis. Inhaled tobramycin and colistin are essential for eradication and maintenance.

left.title: Early Childhood Pathogens (<6 Years)
points: Staphylococcus aureus (sensitive and MRSA)
Non-typeable Haemophilus influenzae
Treat with oral co-amoxiclav or flucloxacillin
Prevent irreversible early airway architectural damage

right.title: Late Childhood & Adolescence Pathogens
points: Mucoid Pseudomonas aeruginosa (alginate biofilm)
Burkholderia cepacia complex (cepacia syndrome)
Achromobacter xylosoxidans and non-tuberculous mycobacteria
Requires inhaled aminoglycosides and IV ceftazidime

steps.tx: Novel small-molecule modulators restore gating and protein folding to mutant CFTR channels. Transformative modern therapy deploys **CFTR modulator therapies**, including the channel potentiator ivacaftor and chaperone correctors lumacaftor, tezacaftor, and elexacaftor. Triple combination therapy (elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor) significantly improves lung function, drops sweat chloride concentrations below the diagnostic threshold, improves nutritional status, and slows long-term pulmonary architectural decline.
steps.say: Small-molecule CFTR modulators like ivacaftor and elexacaftor correct the underlying channel defect, dropping sweat chloride and dramatically improving lung function.
